incidente.resumo: In US-EAST-1, an automated capacity-scaling activity triggered unexpected behavior from many internal-network clients, which a latent issue kept from backing off; the connection surge and retries congested the devices linking the internal and main AWS networks, impairing control-plane APIs, monitoring, console logins and dependent services. Operators moved internal DNS traffic, identified top traffic sources to isolate, disabled heavy services and added capacity; network devices recovered by 2:22 PM PST, some services later.

gatilho.texto: At 7:30 AM PST, an automated activity to scale capacity of one of the AWS services hosted in the main AWS network triggered an unexpected behavior from a large number of clients inside the internal network.
trechos: At 7:30 AM PST, an automated activity to scale capacity of one of the AWS services hosted in the main AWS network triggered an unexpected behavior from a large number of clients inside the internal network.

descricao.texto: A latent issue in a long-standing code path prevented the networking clients from adequately backing off; the resulting large surge of connection activity overwhelmed the networking devices between the internal network and the main AWS network, delaying communication between the networks.
trechos: Our networking clients have well tested request back-off behaviors that are designed to allow our systems to recover from these sorts of congestion events, but, a latent issue prevented these clients from adequately backing off during this event.
This code path has been in production for many years but the automated scaling activity triggered a previously unobserved behavior.

This resulted in a large surge of connection activity that overwhelmed the networking devices between the internal network and the main AWS network, resulting in delays for communication between these networks.

This led to persistent congestion and performance issues on the devices connecting the two networks.

fatores_contribuintes.texto: Many API Gateway servers got into a state where they needed replacement, which normally happens through an automated recycling process that was not possible until the EC2 APIs began recovering; errors remained elevated while the process worked through the backlog.
trechos: As a result of these errors, many API Gateway servers eventually got into a state where they needed to be replaced in order to serve requests successfully.
This normally happens through an automated recycling process, but this was not possible until the EC2 APIs began recovering.

While API Gateways began seeing recovery at 1:35 PM PST, errors and latencies remained elevated as API Gateway capacity was recycled by the automated process working through the backlog of affected servers.

passos.texto: Internal DNS traffic, which was believed to be contributing to the congestion, was moved away from the congested network paths; the work was completed at 9:28 AM PST, DNS resolution errors fully recovered and load on the networking devices was reduced, but congestion was not eliminated.
trechos: Because internal DNS is foundational for all services and this traffic was believed to be contributing to the congestion, the teams focused on moving the internal DNS traffic away from the congested network paths.
At 9:28 AM PST, the team completed this work and DNS resolution errors fully recovered.
This change improved the availability of several impacted services by reducing load on the impacted networking devices, but did not fully resolve the AWS service impact or eliminate the congestion.

passos.texto: Operators applied remediation actions to reduce congestion on the internal network, including identifying the top sources of traffic to isolate to dedicated network devices, disabling some heavy network traffic services, and bringing additional networking capacity online; congestion significantly improved by 1:34 PM PST and all network devices fully recovered by 2:22 PM PST.
trechos: Operators continued working on a set of remediation actions to reduce congestion on the internal network including identifying the top sources of traffic to isolate to dedicated network devices, disabling some heavy network traffic services, and bringing additional networking capacity online.
As the operations teams continued applying the remediation actions described above, congestion significantly improved by 1:34 PM PST, and all network devices fully recovered by 2:22 PM PST.

passos.texto: To reduce load on the affected network devices, event delivery for EventBridge was disabled at 12:35 PM and re-enabled at 2:35 PM PST.
trechos: However, during mitigation efforts to reduce the load on the affected network devices, operators disabled event delivery for EventBridge at 12:35 PM.
Event delivery was re-enabled at 2:35 PM PST, however the service experienced elevated event delivery latency until 6:40 PM PST as it processed the backlog of events.

trechos: The API Gateway team is working on a set of mitigations to ensure that API Gateway servers remain healthy even when the internal network is unavailable and making improvements to the recycling process to speed recovery efforts in the event of a similar issue in the future.

The definition 'from the start of the impact to recovery' is satisfied by both the recovery of the network devices and the recovery of the last dependent service, and the text states no single impact duration.
observacoes: categoria_causa is software-bug rather than capacity-load because the text attributes the failure to a latent client back-off issue; mudanca_causadora is nao_se_aplica because the trigger was an automated scaling activity, not a persistent change.
